name: Title card
signature: Full-screen moss backdrop, plated lockup alone, scroll cue, no words
description: The quietest composition: full-bleed 'moss-hung trunks' photo backdrop with the plated Mittagong Mycology lockup alone and a scroll cue — no headline, no buttons. Shared cream-on-forest type and grain overlay of the whole lab.

name: Logo + headline
signature: Lockup then a single headline beneath, no buttons
description: Lockup on the moss backdrop with one Fraunces headline beneath ('Mushrooms grown slow in the Highlands cold') and nothing else — no CTAs. A middle weight between the bare title card and the full hero.

name: Full hero
signature: Lockup, headline, sub, brick primary + ghost CTA pair, scroll cue
description: The complete stack: plated lockup, Fraunces headline, Archivo sub about the Mittagong farm, a brick primary CTA ('See this week's harvest') beside a ghost CTA ('Visit the farm'), and a scroll cue over the shared backdrop.

name: Splash → resolve
signature: Starts as the c1 title card; on first scroll the lockup shrinks aside while headline and CTAs assemble around it
description: A two-stage composition that opens as the pure title card, then on first scroll the lockup shrinks and moves aside while the headline and CTAs assemble around it — a splash screen that resolves into the full hero.

name: Stacked hero
signature: Mark above wordmark at every width — the phone layout kept on desktop rather than unstacked
description: Phone-first composition: the lockup stays stacked (mark above wordmark) at every viewport, headline beneath — the container-query-driven phone layout deliberately kept on desktop. Driven by the shared lockup primitive's shell width.

name: Mark as bullet
signature: Bare glyph as a typographic bullet on the eyebrow; an oversized wordmark carries the hero — no lockup at all
description: No lockup: the bare glyph (no plate) acts as a typographic mark on the eyebrow line while an oversized wordmark carries the hero. One of the eight plate-less options.

name: Split
signature: Lockup one side, words the other; collapses to one column on phone where the lockup restacks
description: Split composition: the plated lockup sits on one side and the words on the other; on phone it falls to a single column and the lockup restacks itself via the shared container-query primitive.

name: Watermark
signature: Oversized bare glyph as texture behind the headline; the small complete plated lockup keeps its plate in the corner
description: An oversized bare glyph is used as texture behind the Fraunces headline while a small complete lockup with its brick plate sits in the corner — the mark at two scales at once.

name: Edge-anchored
signature: Lockup pinned to a corner, words set asymmetrically against it
description: Asymmetric composition: the bare-glyph lockup (no plate) is pinned to a corner and the headline/words are set off-grid against it — a deliberately unbalanced editorial layout.

name: Spore-drop & gill-unfurl
signature: Spore drops and settles, four blades unfurl downward from their apexes, wordmark rises letter by letter
description: The lab's signature botanical entrance: the spore drops and settles, the glyph's four blades unfurl downward from their apexes, then the wordmark rises letter by letter. CSS keyframes only, replayable.

name: Mist-resolve
signature: Whole lockup resolves out of blur as if mist clears — played on the bare glyph
description: The entire lockup resolves out of a blur, as if the forest mist clears — run on the bare glyph with nothing behind it so the plate itself can be judged against its plated neighbour.

name: Ink draw-on
signature: Blades self-draw as lines, fill floods in, letters wipe left to right; the slowest entrance with a skip control
description: The line-art entrance: the blades self-draw as strokes, the fill floods in, then the letters wipe left to right. Deliberately the slowest of the fifteen and the only one with a skip control.

name: Rise from ground
signature: Everything rises from below a horizon with staggered letters; the bare glyph breaks the line as a shape, not a slab
description: The whole lockup rises from below a horizon line, letters staggered — played on the bare glyph so the mark breaks the letter row as an organic shape rather than a brick slab.

name: Blades assemble
signature: Four blades fly in from the corners and lock into the grid; the spore lands last
description: A construction entrance: the glyph's four blades fly in from the screen corners and lock into the grid, with the spore dropping in as the final piece.

name: Plate & punch
signature: Plate scales in as a slab, glyph punches through it, letters snap, brick dot lands with a bounce
description: The new moving parts on show: the brick plate scales in as a slab, the glyph punches through it, the letters snap into place and the red full stop lands last with a bounce.

name: Letterpress stamp
signature: Ink-bleed blur sharpening with slight per-letter rotation; the dot stamps last
description: A print-shop entrance: each letter arrives with an ink-bleed blur that sharpens and a slight rotation, like letterpress type being stamped; the brick full stop stamps down last.

name: Colony bloom
signature: Radial mask expands from the spore outward across plate then wordmark, like a colony spreading on agar
description: A radial mask expands outward from the spore across the plate and then the wordmark, like a mycological colony spreading on agar; direction re-aims between stacked and row orientations.

name: Thread & pop
signature: A mycelial thread draws along the letter row, each letter pops as it is reached, the dot is the terminal node — bare glyph throughout
description: A mycelial thread draws along the letter row and each letter pops as the thread reaches it, ending at the brick full stop as the terminal node. Runs bare — the thread grows out of the mark, not across a tile.

name: Plate flip
signature: Plate turns on its own vertical axis, blank edge first, glyph revealed on landing, letters cascade after
description: The brick plate turns on its own vertical axis — blank edge first — with the glyph revealed as it lands face-on; the wordmark letters cascade in afterwards.

name: Zoom through the spore
signature: Opens inside the spore and pulls back out to the full plated lockup
description: A camera-move entrance: the view opens inside the spore circle and pulls back out to reveal the complete plated lockup. (Its scroll-side twin is s6.)

name: Centre-out radiate
signature: Blades radiate from the mark's centre and the plate expands in behind them last — bare glyph for most of the run
description: The glyph's blades radiate outward from the mark's centre and the brick plate expands in behind them as the final beat — the lockup runs bare for most of its length and only plates at the end.

name: Plate wipe
signature: A band of brick sweeps across with the glyph knocked out of it, leaving the plate behind as it goes
description: A band of brick red sweeps across the lockup with the glyph knocked out of it like a stencil, and the band leaves the plate behind as it passes — the plate deposited by the wipe itself.

name: Write then slam
signature: Wordmark writes itself bare first, then the plate slams in behind the mark and kicks the lockup as it lands
description: A two-beat entrance: the wordmark writes itself first with no plate at all, then the brick plate slams in behind the mark and physically kicks the lockup as it lands.

name: Stack-to-row
signature: Begins stacked (mark above wordmark) and resolves into the row lockup
description: The lockup begins stacked — mark above wordmark — and animates into the horizontal row lockup as its resolution; the whole premise is the orientation flip owned by the shared lockup primitive.

name: Wordmark retracts, mark survives
signature: Letters retract in reverse stagger while the mark shrinks into the header slot
description: Scroll behaviour on the lab's shared ~250vh parallax stage: the wordmark letters retract in reverse stagger while the plated mark shrinks down into the header slot.

name: Full FLIP fly-to-header
signature: The whole lockup travels, scales and lands in the header bar as one scroll-linked move (GSAP Flip)
description: The entire plated lockup travels, scales and lands in the header bar as one continuous scroll-linked move, powered by GSAP Flip — no separate header logo swap.

name: Parallax drift + fade
signature: Lockup drifts up slower than the page and fades; a separate header logo fades in
description: The gentlest exit: the plated lockup drifts upward slower than the page and fades out while a separate header logo fades in to take its place.

name: Scale-through mask
signature: Lockup scales up and the brick plate's own rounded square becomes the mask the next section is revealed through
description: The lockup scales up toward the viewer and the brick plate's rounded square itself becomes the aperture through which the next section is revealed — the plate is the transition.

name: Pin & hold
signature: Lockup pins centre-screen while the backdrop scrubs past, then releases
description: The plated lockup pins dead centre while the moss backdrop scrubs past it, holding the brand still against the motion before releasing the page.

name: Zoom through the spore
signature: Viewport travels into the spore, whose circle is the aperture the next section arrives through
description: The scroll-side twin of e11: the viewport travels into the spore on scroll and the spore's circle becomes the aperture through which the next section arrives.

name: Re-orient on the way up
signature: Starts stacked and resolves into a row as it shrinks into the header
description: As you scroll away, the stacked lockup resolves into a row while shrinking into the header slot — the orientation flip performed in reverse as the exit move.

name: Plate becomes the bar
signature: The brick plate detaches from the mark and expands into the header background
description: The most graphic handoff: the brick plate detaches from the mark and stretches out to become the header bar itself — the brand colour literally becomes the chrome.

name: Letters disperse
signature: The seventeen letters scatter individually on their own paths, leaving the bare mark
description: All seventeen wordmark letters scatter individually on their own paths as you scroll away, leaving only the bare glyph behind — a spore-drift exit on the plate-less mark.

name: Recede in depth
signature: Lockup rotates and scales away on a 3D axis rather than travelling up the page
description: Instead of travelling up the page, the bare-glyph lockup rotates and scales away on a 3D perspective axis — receding into depth as the page scrolls on.

name: Direction-aware
signature: Header appears on scroll-up, hides on scroll-down
description: The classic behaviour: the plated-mark header appears when you scroll up and hides again when you scroll down. In this gallery the plate marker describes the header's own mark, not the hero's.

name: Appears at hero exit
signature: Header slides down once past ~80vh, then stays
description: The header stays out of the hero's way entirely, then slides down once the page passes roughly 80vh and remains fixed from then on.

name: Hairline first
signature: A rule draws across the top edge first, then the contents fade in beneath it
description: A quiet, editorial arrival: a single hairline rule draws across the top edge of the viewport and the header contents fade in beneath it afterwards.

name: Frosted bar materialises
signature: Header and its frosted backdrop arrive together, blur capped at 12px
description: The header materialises together with its frosted translucent backdrop — glass over the moss photo, with the backdrop blur deliberately capped at 12px.

name: Grows from the plate
signature: The bar bleeds out of the mark's brick plate and spreads across the width
description: The bar appears to be born from the logo itself: it bleeds out of the mark's brick plate and spreads across the full width — the brand colour seeding the chrome.

name: Orientation swap
signature: A stacked mini-lockup on phone, a row lockup on desktop
description: The header's arrival varies the mark's orientation rather than the motion: a stacked mini-lockup on phone, a row lockup on desktop, sharing the container-query primitive with the rest of the lab.

name: Enters from the side
signature: Slides in horizontally from the left edge rather than dropping from the top
description: The one header that varies only direction: it slides in horizontally from the left edge instead of dropping from the top, everything else identical to its siblings.

name: Nav staggers in
signature: Bar arrives first, then the nav items and the CTA individually
description: A choreographed arrival: the header bar lands first, then each nav item and finally the CTA drop in individually with a stagger.

name: Dot as accent
signature: The brick full stop used as a live accent in the bar, beside a bare glyph
description: The header's mark runs bare and the brick full stop from the wordmark is promoted to a live accent element in the bar — the tiniest possible brand gesture carrying the header.
